      "observations": [
        "The landing routes copying, display and streaming through an EWS nsIChannel, downloading into the offline store first when necessary. The common proxy substitutes the actual channel for the input-stream pump request because docshell expects a channel. mShouldStart is cleared before forwarding the first start, so it records whether notification is still owed rather than whether the operation is active. The review explicitly explains this rename and the listener-abort reason; deleted default/copy constructors are applied.",
        "Setup failure from AsyncReadMessageFromStore returns synchronously through AsyncOpen. Failures after AsyncOpen returns need listener callbacks. The historical fetch stop chains store/header writes to reach OnDownloadFinished, but passes original status rather than local rv; the existing static concern remains. Fixed source uses ExchangeFetchMsgsToOffline, propagates status=rv after store/header updates, and the channel sends start/stop for asynchronous fetch/read-start failure. These later endpoint differences are comparison context, not original patch credit or a proof that every failure path is correct.",
        "The downloaded offline byte count replaces trusting the server size in this landing. Fixed MsgFetcher now keeps server messageSize separate and writes only offlineMessageSize; reuse the existing size-contract lesson. Raw message bytes do not establish UTF-8. The initial charset is empty, while a later SetContentType fallback can set UTF-8; the review’s raw-byte distinction must not be broadened into a claim that charset always stays empty.",
        "The review keeps OnFetchStop after the author explains failure-compatible naming, and rejects an aMoveMessage assertion because callers may copy as part of a move. Callback-origin comments and onFetchedDataAvailable apply across IDL/C++/Rust. Global URI naming/interface simplification and true streaming remain deferred. Protocol/common placement is an accepted scoped architecture choice, not a repository-wide relocation rule.",
        "The reviewer explicitly withdraws blanket member nsAutoCString advice. Final member choices use nsAutoCStringN<255> for content type and nsAutoCString for charset, with size rationale. The reviewer’s success/output-value expectation is explicitly aspirational and acknowledges XPCOM exceptions. One unused OrFlags output zero-init question remains Not Done; approval does not prove that question was adopted.",
        "Fixed source stores flags/group before a read request and reapplies them after creating it. Download-phase Cancel/Suspend/Resume remain unavailable; cached-read requests delegate. Existing cancellation, pending/status, security-listener and URI-query static questions stay investigations, with no new failure or security claim. Current discard behavior is preference-gated and clears channel ownership after stop, unlike the original unconditional discard.",
        "The full tracker explains the original quoting double-conversion and a discarded interface-query workaround. The author reports an attachment re-render loop with this patch alone and says the stacked attachment patch removes it; both Bugs explicitly request coordinated landing. Manual account/network instructions are not a test run here. Neither landing changes tests; current EWS/Graph raw-fetch assertions are later comparison coverage and do not prove cancellation, setup/async failures or display."
      ],

      "observations": [
        "The attachment patch passes a convert flag into the channel and the offline helper. Ordinary display leaves initial conversion to docshell; explicit part= or convert=true requests run the message/rfc822 converter first, allowing a later PDF.js conversion for a PDF part. Raw streaming stays separate. The literal-spec conversion checks remain distinct from the newer parsed attachment-disposition helper; existing encoded/substrings questions are unverified investigations.",
        "The channel implements property-bag support and mutable content disposition/length, initially inline and unknown length(-1); unavailable filename/header accessors return NS_ERROR_NOT_AVAILABLE. The MIME emitter now falls back to the original URI spec when it cannot query a MailNews URL, while the news-specific originalSpec route remains separate. No generic MIME or every-protocol behavior claim.",
        "GetUrlForUri preserves the query while moving the message key from fragment to path and changing the internal scheme. StreamMessage appends & only when query content already exists, then convert=true without a leading question mark. The reviewer requests exactly that query-setter correction and the author acknowledges it; both landed and fixed source apply it. Fixed source also appends optional header and supports Graph, later endpoint comparison only.",
        "FetchMimePart accepts the internal URI, returns it and delegates to the shared FetchMessage channel-opening path. Its expected scheme check is a debug assertion, not release validation. Registered x-moz-ews message-service routing supports this path. Fixed attachment disposition uses parsed part/type values with case-insensitive message/PDF exceptions, replacing the landing’s duplicated literal whitelist.",
        "The Bug first lands a Gecko remoteness-policy patch, then is reopened because leave-open was omitted while the comm attachment work remained. That reopening is not a backout. Both Bugs request the channel/attachment patches land together. No independent Gecko source audit or paired-checkout claim follows from the tracker.
